factors.name: Size and branching volume
factors.summary: The largest factor (39.8% of variance) combines net size with counts of splitting and parallel structure: empty sequence flows (0.95), Size (0.86), Token split (0.82), Connector Mismatch (0.75) and Control flow complexity (0.72). It reflects how large a net is and how much branching it contains in absolute terms. Token split (0.48 on Factor 2) and Size (0.45 on Factor 3) also have secondary loadings, and Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factor 2 (0.64).

factors.name: Connectivity and connector degree
factors.summary: Factor 2 (23.5% of variance) is carried by Maximum connector degree (0.88) and Coefficient of network connectivity (0.83), with Control flow complexity as a cross-loading (0.64). It captures how many arcs attach to nodes, both on average and at the busiest connector, largely independent of size. Coefficient of network connectivity also loads 0.44 on Factor 1.

factors.name: Sparseness and separability
factors.summary: Factor 3 (14.9% of variance, eigenvalue only just above 1) contrasts low Density (-0.78) with high Separability (0.61), so it describes sparse, loosely coupled nets with many non-articulation nodes. Size loads 0.45 here, consistent with Density shrinking as nets grow, since its denominator is 2·|T|·|P|. Sequentiality's loading (-0.35) is weak, barely larger than its loadings on Factors 1 and 2 (about 0.31), and should not be used to name the factor.

interpretation.overall: The data are suitable for factor analysis (Bartlett p < 0.001, overall KMO 0.82). Three varimax-rotated factors explain 78% of the variance, matching the suggested factor count. The structure separates absolute size and branching volume (Factor 1) from arc-per-node connectivity (Factor 2) and from a sparseness/separability dimension (Factor 3). The first factor dominates. Control flow complexity bridges Factors 1 and 2, and Sequentiality is poorly represented by the solution (communality 0.32).
caveats: Control flow complexity cross-loads on Factor 1 (0.72) and Factor 2 (0.64), so it does not cleanly belong to either.
Sequentiality has a low communality (0.32) and similar small loadings on all three factors, so its assignment to Factor 3 is weak.
The third eigenvalue (1.06) is close to 1, so Factor 3 may not be stable across datasets or factor counts.
Connector Heterogeneity and Average connector degree were removed by the MSA filter, and Number of duplicate tasks was constant, so these aspects are not represented.

The factors describe shared variance among nets discovered in this dataset of 288 models and depend on the discovery algorithms, the rotation and the chosen factor count; they do not imply causal relations.
